I will keep my land in the usual `winter wheat -> summer maize` rotation. I am in Quzhou County on the south Hebei plain, and that rotation matches my soil, water, machinery rhythm, and the market I know best. At the start of this season, the winter wheat is already in the field, so I would not change crops now. I would focus on managing the wheat steadily through spring, then turn the field quickly into summer maize after harvest. I would not split land into too many crops, because at my age I want a system I can run reliably with mechanized work, fewer labor peaks, and less marketing risk.

For the wheat, I would stay with an improved local variety, keep fertilizer moderate but not light, and irrigate around the key stages instead of watering blindly. I would watch seedling vigor and soil moisture, then put most of the nitrogen from jointing onward so the crop stands well and fills grain. I would spray only as needed around spring disease and insect pressure and again near heading and flowering if conditions turn risky. After wheat harvest, I would go straight into hybrid summer maize with no-tillage direct seeding to save time and preserve moisture. On maize, I would push for even emergence, keep density and water stable, and move nitrogen later into the main growth period. I would accept a slightly conservative but dependable target yield rather than chase demonstration-field numbers.
